pr.title: Draw the panel from the watch daemon and deliver its events
pr.head: d4fcbc92f39f74547c1a9925d6af58debec32575

summary: Projector's panel is the area Claude Code draws above the prompt, listing the pull requests a session works on and its inbox. Until now it found those pull requests by spotting the commands that started a watcher script, watch-threads.sh or watch-prs.sh, and asked GitHub about all of them every 30 seconds. The layers below this one replace those watchers with one watch daemon per machine. A session subscribes to a pull request by writing a line to its own subscriptions file, and the daemon queries GitHub, caches each result, and appends events, such as a new finding or a conflict, to the session's events file.
In Claude Code, nothing yet put those events in front of the agent, and the panel still ran its own GitHub query. This layer closes both gaps in the plugin's mod, the hooks module in hooks/:

• Delivery. At session start and once a minute, the mod runs project watch renew --deliverer mod, which marks the session live and starts the daemon. Every 5 seconds it checks the events file, and when it holds lines, runs project watch take --json and submits them as one prompt.
  • Subscribing on push. After a Bash call that runs git push, gh pr create, or gh stack, the mod sends the output to project watch add --from-output -.
  • The panel. It lists the session's subscriptions, plus the pull requests the daemon adopted for a whole-repository review subscription, reading each row from the daemon's cache and the operator from daemon.json. A drawer names the roles, fixing and reviewing, and dismiss runs project watch drop per role.
A session that started an old watcher before the upgrade keeps it, and only those pull requests still cost the panel a GitHub query.

cards.title: The daemon's files the mod reads
cards.html:
File, under ~/.local/state/projector/watch/What the mod does with it
sessions/<id>/subscriptionsLists the pull requests and roles; ! lines exclude one
sessions/<id>/state.jsonReads adopted, the pull requests a repository subscription covers
sessions/<id>/eventsStats it each tick and takes it when not empty
cache/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<n>.jsonDraws the row; a missing file draws loading…
daemon.jsonReads operator to sort your own pull requests first

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• The first review, at d4fcbc9, opened two findings: the panel ignores ! lines for adopted pull requests, so a dismissed one stays until the daemon's next pass, and after /clear the new session id waits up to a minute for its first renewal.
  • The full gate passed, and hooks/typecheck.sh passed against the main checkout's declarations.

groups.title: Reading the daemon's files
groups.kicker: Pure parsers for the subscriptions, adopted list, operator, cache, and push commands
intro: These functions turn the daemon's files into what the panel draws, with no engine calls, so hooks/parse.test.ts can test each one alone. A subscription line reads like owner/repo#12 fix, owner/repo#12 review <model> <reviewer>, or owner/repo review <model> <reviewer> for every pull request of a repository. A leading ! keeps that pull request out of the role.
parseCache reuses toPullRequest, the function that already reads the panel's own GraphQL answer, because the daemon caches the same node shape with every field the panel draws.

files.note: Adds the subscription grammar, subscribedOf, the readers of state.json and daemon.json, the state-root and cache paths, and isPushCommand.

checks.text: Open finding: adopted pull requests skip the ! check, so a dismissed adopted pull request stays listed until the daemon's next pass, up to watch.interval seconds. Models in ! lines are compared exactly, not by the daemon's lowercased identity without a [1m]-style variant.
The cache path lowercases the repository, as the daemon's cache_dir does, and the state root follows XDG_STATE_HOME as watch.state_root does.
The daemon's QUERY asks for every field toPullRequest reads, including updatedAt, additions, deletions, and changedFiles, so a cached row keeps its age and changed lines. Checked by reading both.

files.note: Adds the Role type, a row's roles in place of its loop kinds, isLoading, and the panelSubscribed state key, which claude plugin validate . requires.

groups.title: Delivering events and drawing the panel
groups.kicker: The mod renews the session, submits events, subscribes on push, and draws rows from the cache
intro: Every 5-second tick now runs checkWatch whether or not the panel is shown: it delivers events, renews the session when a minute passed with none, and shows the panel when a new subscription appears. A shown panel also reloads its rows from the files on every tick. It asks GitHub only every 30 seconds, and only for an old watcher's pull requests that the daemon has no result for.

isSubmitting holds back the next take while a submitted prompt waits for the session, so events that arrive meanwhile go as one later prompt. take empties the file under the session's lock, so each event is delivered once.

files.note: Adds renew, deliverEvents, noticeSubscriptions, checkWatch, and subscribeFrom; rewrites load to read the daemon's files, dismissPr to drop by role, and the row and drawer for loading rows and roles.

checks.text: Open finding: renewedAt is not keyed by session id, so after /clear or a resume moves the session to a new id, that id goes unrenewed for up to a minute, and a skill's project watch add in that window reports events: none and starts a second deliverer.
The Bash hook passes the output to project watch add --from-output - without waiting, so a push's result never waits on GitHub.

groups.title: Tests
groups.kicker: Parser cases and simulated-engine panel cases for the daemon's files
intro: parse.test.ts covers the grammar, exclusions, adopted lists, and push detection. panel.test.tsx adds watchWorld, a simulated engine whose project watch commands edit in-memory files as the CLI would, and uses it to test listing, delivery, renewal, push subscription, and dismissal.

checks.text: claude plugin test . ran 212 tests at this head with none failing.

groups.title: Documentation and plans
groups.kicker: The panel's guide, the fixing role in panel-themes, and what the mod settled
intro: docs/plugins.md describes the panel's new sources, the loading row, dismiss by role, and a new section on how the mod delivers events. The panel-themes plan, a draft, renames its watching role to fixing. The watch-daemon plan, in progress, appends § 9.3 with the choices this layer settled.

§ 9.3 is appended after § 9.2, and the one in-place edit, in § 3, renumbers nothing.
